It closes the “garage prop” gap with a named production asset rather than an invisible placeholder, a recycled generic puff, an unrelated object, or a crude primitive approximation. The result must communicate its purpose immediately through silhouette, motion, timing, optical response, state, surface contact, or interaction while following maintained premium residential design with refined stone, glass, metal, landscaping, quiet luxury, and discreet service access.

Required production anatomy: object-specific primary body, support or contact structure, functional opening or access, handle, control, or closure, secondary functional assembly, fasteners and seams, placement contact, interaction or inventory socket. Every component is functional. Components connect through believable supports, timing relationships, strand roots, anatomy, attachment points, projection rules, emitter origins, service paths, collision-safe boundaries, or state transitions appropriate to Rich Hills garage Package Medium Standard. Materials and response layers include primary structural material, secondary functional material, hardware or closure material, transparent, flexible, organic, or emissive material when needed. Separation follows real construction, biological growth, light transport, contamination, weather, particle behavior, hair-fiber behavior, or gameplay state rather than arbitrary color blocks.

Implementation defines a stable named origin, deterministic forward or projection direction, scale envelope, spawn or placement conditions, looping or one-shot lifecycle, transition timing, cleanup and pooling, network relevance, quality tiers, editor-preview metadata, and validation thresholds. Dependencies on surfaces, bodies, vehicles, weapons, water, wind, camera, lighting, audio, quests, or interaction sockets are explicit and testable. Close-range presentation needs convincing breakup, thickness, depth, hardware, strand structure, species anatomy, or layered motion. Distant presentation preserves the primary read without excessive triangles, overdraw, alpha sorting, particle count, shadows, or replication traffic.

Accessibility is mandatory. The asset does not rely on color alone. Flashing, injury feedback, camera motion, particle density, and hazard communication include reduced-flash, reduced-motion, reduced-particle, high-contrast, or icon alternatives where relevant. Injury effects default to non-graphic presentation. Stylized blood is abstract and optional, contains no gore or exposed anatomy, and has paint, spark, dust, and comic-impact alternatives. Afros are not bunched spheres. Locs are not identical cylinders. Braids and twists show interwoven rhythm, parting, tension, taper, and purposeful styling.

This specification never authorizes crude geometry. It closes the “garage runtime-vfx” gap with a named production asset rather than an invisible placeholder, a recycled generic puff, an unrelated object, or a crude primitive approximation. The result must communicate its purpose immediately through silhouette, motion, timing, optical response, state, surface contact, or interaction while following maintained premium residential design with refined stone, glass, metal, landscaping, quiet luxury, and discreet service access.

Required production anatomy: named emitter origin, primary particle or optical layer, secondary breakup layer, timing envelope, surface or volume response, quality tiers, pooling and cleanup rule, reduced-motion and reduced-flash alternative. Every component is functional. Components connect through believable supports, timing relationships, strand roots, anatomy, attachment points, projection rules, emitter origins, service paths, collision-safe boundaries, or state transitions appropriate to Rich Hills garage Window Reflection Sweep Standard. Materials and response layers include particle sprite or procedural field, optical or emissive layer, surface-response mask, accessibility fallback. Separation follows real construction, biological growth, light transport, contamination, weather, particle behavior, hair-fiber behavior, or gameplay state rather than arbitrary color blocks.

Implementation defines a stable named origin, deterministic forward or projection direction, scale envelope, spawn or placement conditions, looping or one-shot lifecycle, transition timing, cleanup and pooling, network relevance, quality tiers, editor-preview metadata, and validation thresholds. Dependencies on surfaces, bodies, vehicles, weapons, water, wind, camera, lighting, audio, quests, or interaction sockets are explicit and testable. Close-range presentation needs convincing breakup, thickness, depth, hardware, strand structure, species anatomy, or layered motion. Distant presentation preserves the primary read without excessive triangles, overdraw, alpha sorting, particle count, shadows, or replication traffic.

Accessibility is mandatory. The asset does not rely on color alone. Flashing, injury feedback, camera motion, particle density, and hazard communication include reduced-flash, reduced-motion, reduced-particle, high-contrast, or icon alternatives where relevant. Injury effects default to non-graphic presentation. Stylized blood is abstract and optional, contains no gore or exposed anatomy, and has paint, spark, dust, and comic-impact alternatives. Hair uses a scalp-conforming root field, purposeful hairline, believable density and gravity, style-specific structure, silhouette variation, ear and nape clearance, recolor support, and secondary-motion planning. Afros are not bunched spheres. Locs are not identical cylinders. Braids and twists show interwoven rhythm, parting, tension, taper, and purposeful styling.

This specification never authorizes crude geometry. Every layer reinforces Rich Hills garage Window Reflection Sweep Standard, integrates with adjacent Zaylins systems, and passes recognition, lifecycle, town-style, accessibility, performance, and state review. It closes the “landscape decal” gap with a named production asset rather than an invisible placeholder, a recycled generic puff, an unrelated object, or a crude primitive approximation. The result must communicate its purpose immediately through silhouette, motion, timing, optical response, state, surface contact, or interaction while following maintained premium residential design with refined stone, glass, metal, landscaping, quiet luxury, and discreet service access.

Required production anatomy: projection boundary, primary mark silhouette, secondary edge breakup, opacity mask, surface normal response, scale variation, fade lifecycle, clean or child-safe alternative. Every component is functional. Components connect through believable supports, timing relationships, strand roots, anatomy, attachment points, projection rules, emitter origins, service paths, collision-safe boundaries, or state transitions appropriate to Rich Hills landscape Dry Footprint Standard. Materials and response layers include vector color layer, opacity mask, roughness response, normal or height suggestion. Separation follows real construction, biological growth, light transport, contamination, weather, particle behavior, hair-fiber behavior, or gameplay state rather than arbitrary color blocks.

Implementation defines a stable named origin, deterministic forward or projection direction, scale envelope, spawn or placement conditions, looping or one-shot lifecycle, transition timing, cleanup and pooling, network relevance, quality tiers, editor-preview metadata, and validation thresholds. Dependencies on surfaces, bodies, vehicles, weapons, water, wind, camera, lighting, audio, quests, or interaction sockets are explicit and testable. Close-range presentation needs convincing breakup, thickness, depth, hardware, strand structure, species anatomy, or layered motion. Distant presentation preserves the primary read without excessive triangles, overdraw, alpha sorting, particle count, shadows, or replication traffic.

Accessibility is mandatory. The asset does not rely on color alone. Flashing, injury feedback, camera motion, particle density, and hazard communication include reduced-flash, reduced-motion, reduced-particle, high-contrast, or icon alternatives where relevant. Injury effects default to non-graphic presentation. Stylized blood is abstract and optional, contains no gore or exposed anatomy, and has paint, spark, dust, and comic-impact alternatives. Hair uses a scalp-conforming root field, purposeful hairline, believable density and gravity, style-specific structure, silhouette variation, ear and nape clearance, recolor support, and secondary-motion planning. Afros are not bunched spheres. Locs are not identical cylinders. Braids and twists show interwoven rhythm, parting, tension, taper, and purposeful styling.

This specification never authorizes crude geometry. Every layer reinforces Rich Hills landscape Dry Footprint Standard, integrates with adjacent Zaylins systems, and passes recognition, lifecycle, town-style, accessibility, performance, and state review. Rich Hills pool Specular Edge Glint Standard is a procedural-runtime-effect added by the final Zaylins gameplay, sensory, environmental, interaction, customization, and cohesion sweep for rich-hills. It closes the “pool runtime-vfx” gap with a named production asset rather than an invisible placeholder, a recycled generic puff, an unrelated object, or a crude primitive approximation. The result must communicate its purpose immediately through silhouette, motion, timing, optical response, state, surface contact, or interaction while following maintained premium residential design with refined stone, glass, metal, landscaping, quiet luxury, and discreet service access.

Required production anatomy: named emitter origin, primary particle or optical layer, secondary breakup layer, timing envelope, surface or volume response, quality tiers, pooling and cleanup rule, reduced-motion and reduced-flash alternative. Every component is functional. Components connect through believable supports, timing relationships, strand roots, anatomy, attachment points, projection rules, emitter origins, service paths, collision-safe boundaries, or state transitions appropriate to Rich Hills pool Specular Edge Glint Standard. Materials and response layers include particle sprite or procedural field, optical or emissive layer, surface-response mask, accessibility fallback. Separation follows real construction, biological growth, light transport, contamination, weather, particle behavior, hair-fiber behavior, or gameplay state rather than arbitrary color blocks.

Implementation defines a stable named origin, deterministic forward or projection direction, scale envelope, spawn or placement conditions, looping or one-shot lifecycle, transition timing, cleanup and pooling, network relevance, quality tiers, editor-preview metadata, and validation thresholds. Dependencies on surfaces, bodies, vehicles, weapons, water, wind, camera, lighting, audio, quests, or interaction sockets are explicit and testable. Close-range presentation needs convincing breakup, thickness, depth, hardware, strand structure, species anatomy, or layered motion. Distant presentation preserves the primary read without excessive triangles, overdraw, alpha sorting, particle count, shadows, or replication traffic.

Accessibility is mandatory. The asset does not rely on color alone. Flashing, injury feedback, camera motion, particle density, and hazard communication include reduced-flash, reduced-motion, reduced-particle, high-contrast, or icon alternatives where relevant. Injury effects default to non-graphic presentation. Stylized blood is abstract and optional, contains no gore or exposed anatomy, and has paint, spark, dust, and comic-impact alternatives. Hair uses a scalp-conforming root field, purposeful hairline, believable density and gravity, style-specific structure, silhouette variation, ear and nape clearance, recolor support, and secondary-motion planning. Afros are not bunched spheres. Locs are not identical cylinders. Braids and twists show interwoven rhythm, parting, tension, taper, and purposeful styling.

This specification never authorizes crude geometry. Every layer reinforces Rich Hills pool Specular Edge Glint Standard, integrates with adjacent Zaylins systems, and passes recognition, lifecycle, town-style, accessibility, performance, and state review. Required production anatomy: object-specific primary body, support or contact structure, functional opening or access, handle, control, or closure, secondary functional assembly, fasteners and seams, placement contact, interaction or inventory socket. Every component is functional. Components connect through believable supports, timing relationships, strand roots, anatomy, attachment points, projection rules, emitter origins, service paths, collision-safe boundaries, or state transitions appropriate to Rich Hills service Coat On Hook Standard. It closes the “service prop” gap with a named production asset rather than an invisible placeholder, a recycled generic puff, an unrelated object, or a crude primitive approximation. The result must communicate its purpose immediately through silhouette, motion, timing, optical response, state, surface contact, or interaction while following maintained premium residential design with refined stone, glass, metal, landscaping, quiet luxury, and discreet service access.

Required production anatomy: object-specific primary body, support or contact structure, functional opening or access, handle, control, or closure, secondary functional assembly, fasteners and seams, placement contact, interaction or inventory socket. Every component is functional. Components connect through believable supports, timing relationships, strand roots, anatomy, attachment points, projection rules, emitter origins, service paths, collision-safe boundaries, or state transitions appropriate to Rich Hills service Mop Bucket Standard. Materials and response layers include primary structural material, secondary functional material, hardware or closure material, transparent, flexible, organic, or emissive material when needed. Separation follows real construction, biological growth, light transport, contamination, weather, particle behavior, hair-fiber behavior, or gameplay state rather than arbitrary color blocks.

Implementation defines a stable named origin, deterministic forward or projection direction, scale envelope, spawn or placement conditions, looping or one-shot lifecycle, transition timing, cleanup and pooling, network relevance, quality tiers, editor-preview metadata, and validation thresholds. Dependencies on surfaces, bodies, vehicles, weapons, water, wind, camera, lighting, audio, quests, or interaction sockets are explicit and testable. Close-range presentation needs convincing breakup, thickness, depth, hardware, strand structure, species anatomy, or layered motion. Distant presentation preserves the primary read without excessive triangles, overdraw, alpha sorting, particle count, shadows, or replication traffic.

Accessibility is mandatory. The asset does not rely on color alone. Flashing, injury feedback, camera motion, particle density, and hazard communication include reduced-flash, reduced-motion, reduced-particle, high-contrast, or icon alternatives where relevant. Injury effects default to non-graphic presentation. Stylized blood is abstract and optional, contains no gore or exposed anatomy, and has paint, spark, dust, and comic-impact alternatives. Hair uses a scalp-conforming root field, purposeful hairline, believable density and gravity, style-specific structure, silhouette variation, ear and nape clearance, recolor support, and secondary-motion planning. Afros are not bunched spheres. Locs are not identical cylinders. Braids and twists show interwoven rhythm, parting, tension, taper, and purposeful styling.

This specification never authorizes crude geometry. Every layer reinforces Rich Hills service Mop Bucket Standard, integrates with adjacent Zaylins systems, and passes recognition, lifecycle, town-style, accessibility, performance, and state review. It closes the “service prop” gap with a named production asset rather than an invisible placeholder, a recycled generic puff, an unrelated object, or a crude primitive approximation. The result must communicate its purpose immediately through silhouette, motion, timing, optical response, state, surface contact, or interaction while following maintained premium residential design with refined stone, glass, metal, landscaping, quiet luxury, and discreet service access.

Required production anatomy: object-specific primary body, support or contact structure, functional opening or access, handle, control, or closure, secondary functional assembly, fasteners and seams, placement contact, interaction or inventory socket. Every component is functional. Components connect through believable supports, timing relationships, strand roots, anatomy, attachment points, projection rules, emitter origins, service paths, collision-safe boundaries, or state transitions appropriate to Rich Hills service Screwdriver Set Standard. Materials and response layers include primary structural material, secondary functional material, hardware or closure material, transparent, flexible, organic, or emissive material when needed. Separation follows real construction, biological growth, light transport, contamination, weather, particle behavior, hair-fiber behavior, or gameplay state rather than arbitrary color blocks.

Implementation defines a stable named origin, deterministic forward or projection direction, scale envelope, spawn or placement conditions, looping or one-shot lifecycle, transition timing, cleanup and pooling, network relevance, quality tiers, editor-preview metadata, and validation thresholds. Dependencies on surfaces, bodies, vehicles, weapons, water, wind, camera, lighting, audio, quests, or interaction sockets are explicit and testable. Close-range presentation needs convincing breakup, thickness, depth, hardware, strand structure, species anatomy, or layered motion. Distant presentation preserves the primary read without excessive triangles, overdraw, alpha sorting, particle count, shadows, or replication traffic.

Accessibility is mandatory. The asset does not rely on color alone. Flashing, injury feedback, camera motion, particle density, and hazard communication include reduced-flash, reduced-motion, reduced-particle, high-contrast, or icon alternatives where relevant. Injury effects default to non-graphic presentation. Stylized blood is abstract and optional, contains no gore or exposed anatomy, and has paint, spark, dust, and comic-impact alternatives. Hair uses a scalp-conforming root field, purposeful hairline, believable density and gravity, style-specific structure, silhouette variation, ear and nape clearance, recolor support, and secondary-motion planning. Afros are not bunched spheres. Locs are not identical cylinders. Braids and twists show interwoven rhythm, parting, tension, taper, and purposeful styling.

This specification never authorizes crude geometry. Every layer reinforces Rich Hills service Screwdriver Set Standard, integrates with adjacent Zaylins systems, and passes recognition, lifecycle, town-style, accessibility, performance, and state review. Rich Hills wellness Toy Clutter Standard is a dedicated-prop-builder added by the final Zaylins gameplay, sensory, environmental, interaction, customization, and cohesion sweep for rich-hills. It closes the “wellness prop” gap with a named production asset rather than an invisible placeholder, a recycled generic puff, an unrelated object, or a crude primitive approximation. The result must communicate its purpose immediately through silhouette, motion, timing, optical response, state, surface contact, or interaction while following maintained premium residential design with refined stone, glass, metal, landscaping, quiet luxury, and discreet service access.

Required production anatomy: object-specific primary body, support or contact structure, functional opening or access, handle, control, or closure, secondary functional assembly, fasteners and seams, placement contact, interaction or inventory socket. Every component is functional. Components connect through believable supports, timing relationships, strand roots, anatomy, attachment points, projection rules, emitter origins, service paths, collision-safe boundaries, or state transitions appropriate to Rich Hills wellness Toy Clutter Standard. Materials and response layers include primary structural material, secondary functional material, hardware or closure material, transparent, flexible, organic, or emissive material when needed. Separation follows real construction, biological growth, light transport, contamination, weather, particle behavior, hair-fiber behavior, or gameplay state rather than arbitrary color blocks.

Implementation defines a stable named origin, deterministic forward or projection direction, scale envelope, spawn or placement conditions, looping or one-shot lifecycle, transition timing, cleanup and pooling, network relevance, quality tiers, editor-preview metadata, and validation thresholds. Dependencies on surfaces, bodies, vehicles, weapons, water, wind, camera, lighting, audio, quests, or interaction sockets are explicit and testable. Close-range presentation needs convincing breakup, thickness, depth, hardware, strand structure, species anatomy, or layered motion. Distant presentation preserves the primary read without excessive triangles, overdraw, alpha sorting, particle count, shadows, or replication traffic.

Accessibility is mandatory. The asset does not rely on color alone. Flashing, injury feedback, camera motion, particle density, and hazard communication include reduced-flash, reduced-motion, reduced-particle, high-contrast, or icon alternatives where relevant. Injury effects default to non-graphic presentation. Stylized blood is abstract and optional, contains no gore or exposed anatomy, and has paint, spark, dust, and comic-impact alternatives. Hair uses a scalp-conforming root field, purposeful hairline, believable density and gravity, style-specific structure, silhouette variation, ear and nape clearance, recolor support, and secondary-motion planning. Afros are not bunched spheres. Locs are not identical cylinders. Braids and twists show interwoven rhythm, parting, tension, taper, and purposeful styling.

This specification never authorizes crude geometry. Every layer reinforces Rich Hills wellness Toy Clutter Standard, integrates with adjacent Zaylins systems, and passes recognition, lifecycle, town-style, accessibility, performance, and state review. Specialized GLBs remain outside the generic primitive Blender lane until a dedicated builder can satisfy this contract.

Handles, supports, openings, controls, edges, and contact points should explain use.

Acceptance standard: the final model must look intentional from every inspection angle, satisfy every required component, fit the reviewed scale, use meaningful material separation, remain inside geometry budgets, sit correctly on its placement plane, and export as a verified nonempty GLB. Handles, supports, openings, controls, edges, and contact points should explain use.

Acceptance standard: the final model must look intentional from every inspection angle, satisfy every required component, fit the reviewed scale, use meaningful material separation, remain inside geometry budgets, sit correctly on its placement plane, and export as a verified nonempty GLB.
